findings.namedBuyers: Arilda de Oliveira is currently named by the organizer as Founder and Executive Producer: primary production and organizer-relationship contact. Clicia Belmont is identified as marketing director in July 2025 reporting; the matching professional profile is headed CLICIA LIMA and lists current Marketing, Partnerships & Sponsorship Manager at Toronto International BrazilFest from December 2025. She is relevant to sponsorship/partnership discussions; confirm preferred name and current remit. Neither source establishes hotel-contract authority. Request routing through info@brazilfest.ca.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced: July 17–18, 2027, 12 PM–11 PM, Earlscourt Park, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are activity dates, not article timestamps. The official contact page states: “Saturday and Sunday, July 17–18, 2027 · 12 PM – 11 PM.” This corrects the seed’s single-day date. Within the requested horizon. No 2028 edition announcement was identified; do not extrapolate dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could suit a small artist, touring crew, sponsor/VIP or production lodging subset and perhaps an ancillary meeting. The park festival itself is not a hotel ballroom event or resort retreat. A 157-room Harbourfront hotel cannot accommodate the entire festival audience, historically described as thousands; that attendance does not imply overnight demand. The St. Clair/Caledonia venue is outside the hotel’s immediate Harbourfront/MTCC/Exhibition Place catchment, so any lodging pitch needs an agreed transport plan. No room allocation, stay pattern or meeting demand is established; do not turn the hotel’s 15–109-room target range into an event forecast. Catering, restaurant availability and reception feasibility remain unverified.
findings.venueCommitments: Organizer-published 2027 venue: Earlscourt Park, entrance at St. Clair Avenue West and Caledonia Road, Toronto, Ontario. Toronto proper, but in the west-end St. Clair area, not Harbourfront/downtown, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Outdoor public park, not a competing hotel. Announcement establishes the intended event venue; an executed park permit or venue contract was not reviewed. No hotel commitment is established by this park announcement.
findings.historicalRotation: Documented local evolution, not a destination-rotation programme: organizer history places the 2003 debut at Sunnyside Pavilion; the producer’s 2009 announcement explicitly calls Earlscourt Park its “New Location.” The official 2024 preview says the park was also used the previous year. Earlscourt Park is documented for 2024, 2025, 2026 and announced 2027. Annual recurrence is explicit on the current FAQ, not inferred solely from dates. Edition numbers conflict: the 2024 preview says 21st anniversary/edition, the 2024 recap says 19th edition, and 2025 reporting says 20th; use calendar years rather than edition ordinals.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific host hotel, official housing bureau, named contracted hotel, room block, accommodation RFP, room-night commitment or hotel booking link was identified on the reviewed official 2027 pages. Every officially listed accommodation hotel found: none. The official contact route is “Questions? Email us info@brazilfest.ca”; the involvement page invites sponsors to “Explore opportunities to support the festival.” Neither statement is a hotel-sourcing invitation. No published lodging-sourcing statement exists in the reviewed material to quote. A third-party travel article says visitors “should consider these hotels” and mentions discounted rates; this is travel marketing, not evidence of a festival block or incumbent hotel.
findings.organizationStructure: The official privacy policy states: “Toronto International BrazilFest ... is produced by Itabras Entertainment Productions Inc. and Casa Brasil Canada.” Treat this as a producer-led public cultural festival, not an association conference. Arilda is the festival’s founder/executive producer. The reviewed sources do not establish Casa Brasil Canada’s legal/nonprofit status, the ultimate hotel-contracting entity, or any appointed PCO, DMC or housing agency. Earlscourt Park is the venue, not the buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No sourced incumbent hotel, hotel exclusivity, displaced room demand, sellout, overflow requirement or competitive hotel room block was identified. This is not evidence that inventory is open. Main-event venue capture is not the opportunity: the announced programme is in Earlscourt Park. Inference: proximity and transport practicality may disadvantage a Harbourfront property, while a city sightseeing/VIP stay could still appeal to a limited subset. No named competing hotels can responsibly be assigned.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Send a short inquiry to info@brazilfest.ca addressed to Arilda de Oliveira and the partnerships lead, referencing July 17–18, 2027. Ask who contracts artist/crew/VIP accommodation, whether any hotels or agent are already retained, nonlocal headcount, peak rooms, arrival/departure dates, payer, transport and selection deadline. Ask whether Clicia Belmont/CLICIA LIMA remains the partnership contact. Offer only a provisional small-group lodging discussion; do not issue a large block or sponsorship commitment before quantified needs and decision authority are confirmed. Verify restaurant/catering operations internally before proposing hospitality functions. If 2027 is committed or no overnight need exists, obtain permission to revisit the next procurement cycle rather than claim overflow.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The next edition is announced for July 17–18, 2027, but its hotel procurement is unconfirmed. Public organizer email provides relationship access, not proof of an available block. The sponsor page still says “Applications closed” alongside “Sponsorship applications open on November 1”; as of November 16, 2026 this is not reliable evidence of an open application window and must be checked directly. Do not label hotel sourcing open.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: verified annual recurrence supports a relationship-led lodging-partnership conversation for 2027 and later cycles, but not an assumption of future Toronto hotel room demand or a rotating host-hotel contest. Seek only an artist/crew/VIP subset whose travel needs are confirmed. No 2028 dates, future lodging RFP or hotel selection cycle was found. Separate the confirmed 2027 park festival from any speculative future hotel capture.
